## Row {height=86%}

```{r}
#| title: "Live forecasts: log loss of the ensemble vs the benchmark, per horizon"
#| output: asis
if (has_live) {
  live_tab |>
    transmute(Horizon = as.character(h), Quarters = quarters, `Since` = format(dk(from), "%d %b"),
              `Log loss ensemble` = round(ens, 3), `Log loss benchmark` = round(clim, 3),
              `Live skill` = pct(skill, 1)) |>
    knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrr") |>
    cat(sep = "\n")
} else {
  cat("The track record starts once the first forecast quarters have passed.")
}
cat("\n\nEvery forecast is saved before its quarter starts and never changed, and is scored once the",
    "imbalance data for that quarter is published. A few days of live data say little: the backtest",
    "needed months to show differences of a few percent. Want to see the backtest?",
    "<a href=\"backtest.html\"><b>Click here</b></a>.\n")
```

```{r}
#| title: "Live skill so far (lower log loss than the benchmark, cumulative)"
if (has_live) {
  cum <- live |>
    arrange(time) |>
    group_by(horizon) |>
    mutate(skill = 1 - cummean(ll_ens) / cummean(ll_clim), day = as_date(dk(time))) |>
    group_by(horizon, day) |>
    summarise(skill = last(skill), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(h = factor(horizon_labels[horizon], levels = horizon_labels))
  h_colors <- setNames(c("#f97316", "#fb923c", "#fdba74", "#fed7aa", "#2563eb"), horizon_labels)
  plot_ly(cum, x = ~day, y = ~skill, color = ~h, colors = h_colors, type = "scatter",
          mode = "lines+markers", line = list(width = 2.5), marker = list(size = 7),
          hovertemplate = "%{y:.1%}") |>
    chart_layout() |>
    layout(yaxis = list(tickformat = ".0%", zeroline = TRUE),
           xaxis = list(type = "date", tickformat = "%d %b", dtick = 86400000))
} else {
  cat("No scored forecasts yet.")
}
```

# Method

::: {.card title="How it works"}

**What is forecast.** In each quarter-hour, Energinet balances DK1 by activating mFRR reserves up or
down. The direction of that activation sets the imbalance price: usually above the spot price when the
system is short (up-regulation), below it when the system is long (down-regulation), and equal to it
when nothing is activated. The models give the probability of each direction, and a forecast of the spread
between the imbalance price and the spot price.

**When.** Every three hours, for the 16 quarters of the next 4 hours (every hour in the backtest),
using the published imbalance data up to the quarter that started an hour before, and for the first
hour also the real-time state up to ten minutes before (aFRR activation, wind and solar production
against Energinet's forecast, DK1 cross-border flows). Once a day after the day-ahead auction, for all
quarters of tomorrow, using the imbalance data up to noon. For the next hour there is little time left
to trade (cross-border intraday trading closes an hour before delivery), so that forecast is mostly
for assets that can react on their own; two to four hours ahead there is still time to trade on it.

**Inputs.** Hour, quarter, weekday and holidays; the spot price of the quarter (level, negative,
shape over the day); wind and solar forecasts made 48 hours ahead (Open-Meteo); recent imbalances.

**Models.** A multinomial lasso (lambda by BIC), XGBoost, and their average (the ensemble). One model
per hour ahead, trained on the year before and refitted once a week. Benchmark: how often each direction
happened in that hour over the last 28 days.

**Spread.** A mixture: the 300 spreads in up-regulated quarters of the last 60 days with the closest
spot price, weighted by the probability of up, the same for down, and 0 for no regulation. The size of
the spread grows with the spot price, especially for down-regulation.

**Evaluation.** Each test answers one question.

- *Is it better than the benchmark?* Log loss for the direction and pinball loss for the spread, the
  standard scores for probability and quantile forecasts.
- *Is the difference real or luck?* Diebold-Mariano tests on the daily average loss, with a Newey-West
  variance over one week of lags because good and bad days come in runs. The same test, ensemble against
  each model, is why the ensemble is used.
- *Can the probabilities be taken at face value?* The calibration chart: when the forecast says 40%,
  it should happen about 40% of the time.
- *Is it worth anything?* The value of picking a side with the expected spread, since a lower loss
  alone doesn't say that.

The real-time inputs are only used for the first hour because the backtest showed they help there and
not further ahead. Energinet's newer wind and solar forecasts for the hour were tested and made no
difference, most likely because the market already trades on them.

**Backtest:** the scores, tests and calibration are on the [backtest page](backtest.html).

**Data:** [Energi Data Service](https://www.energidataservice.dk) (Energinet), weather by
[Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com).<br>
**Code:** [github.com/jacobazu/dk1-imbalance-forecasting](https://github.com/jacobazu/dk1-imbalance-forecasting)<br>
**Last updated:** `r format(with_tz(Sys.time(), "Europe/Copenhagen"), "%d %B %Y, %H:%M")` (Danish time)

:::
